context.body: The bounded canonical source is Isaiah 49:1–7; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The servant speaks from a call before birth, is named Israel, laments apparently empty labor, and receives a commission to bring Jacob back and become a light to nations.
observations.label: The servant called Israel is sent to restore Israel: action

observations.body: rulers will bow because the Holy One has chosen the servant.

payload.posture: Read Isaiah 49:1–7 as prophets accuse and promise evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The same poem names the servant Israel and gives the servant a mission toward Jacob and Israel without pausing to explain the distinction.
payload.title: The servant called Israel is sent to restore Israel
